UkA6pgt29VI.title: SUP Surf Instruction - How to Paddle Through Breaking Waves
UkA6pgt29VI.description:
In this video ACA SUP Instructor Trainer Jimmy Blakeney gives detailed instruction for getting back out through breaking waves while surfing.

Sponsored by BIC SUP  http://www.bicsup.com

Produced by Heliconia  http://www.helipress.com
UkA6pgt29VI.transcript: Kind: captions Language: en founded in 1979 by the Bick family of bck pen Fame biig sport Grew From a passion for water sports and world renowned expertise in sustainable manufacturing visit big sport.com and learn more about our full range of waterports products one of the most challenging aspects of sub surfing is paddling out through the white water or recovering after you've been caught inside the brake zone so that's what we're going to take a look at in this video we're going to assume that you've already developed a solid foundation of paddling skills because you shouldn't be heading out into the surf zone without them the first thing to mention is how important it is that you be aware of your surroundings as a rule when you're learning to surf or if you're unsure of your ability to control your gear in the surf zone do not surf where there are other Surfers swimmers or even waiters it's simply too dangerous for both you and those around you whether you're recovering from a fall or just paddling out you have three real options for getting through the surf one option is to lie down on your board and paddle out with your paddle on the deck in front of you this can work in smaller waves but big waves will knock you over and wash you back in the best way to deal with big waves from the lying down position is to get off your board push down on the tail and push the board over the foam as you dive under the foam while holding your paddle the second option is to paddle out in a kneeling position and ride over the white Water by leaning back and taking a hard stroke as you hit the foam once again this technique will work in smaller waves but it won't be very effective when waves get over around 3 ft the third and best option for getting out through the surf is to actually stand up and paddle but you need to learn how to punch over the white water first when standing and paddling out through the surf you'll want to assume a hybrid stance with your front foot pointed forwards and your back foot more sideways you'll also want to have your feet slightly staggered one towards the nose and one slightly towards the tail you'll also want to be standing a little further back on your board to make it easier to get the nose on top of the white water when you're punching over the top of waves now what you'll want to do is take a few solid but smooth Strokes on the toe side of your board to create some forward momentum towards the incoming wave having forward momentum is extremely important because without it you're much less stable as the foam approaches you're going to want to keep your center of gravity Low by bending your knees just as the foam is approaching the nose of your board you're going to plant a solid stroke and you're also going to want to put pressure on your back foot don't lean back but put pressure in your back foot keeping your center of gravity over your board you're going to take that stroke and that pressure on the back foot is going to lift the nose over the foam you might find it helpful to move your back foot further back as you do this if all goes as planned your board will skip up onto and over the foam pile the key to making this work is keeping your knees bent and your center of gravity over your board you're going to want to also maintain an active paddle that means you're going to have that paddle blade in the water or you're going to have it on the surface of water acting as a brace if you get knocked off balance you may have to drop to one knee but you'll need to get up as quickly as possible and get ready for the next wave if you're interested in learning more about big standup paddle boards or if you're looking for advice on how to choose the right board for you check us out at bigs.com visit BS up.com and check out the full range of standup paddle boards paddles and accessories

TOP1Fwili-k.title: How To Smash - Badminton Tips
TOP1Fwili-k.description: When your opponent hits the shuttle about two-thirds forward you should smash. In doubles you can smash from the back. When doing the smash, you need to turn sideways using your torso. Reach up, twist your torso and swing across your body. This puts all your power into the racket. It is like thrown a ball downwards. Make sure the contact the shuttle in front of your body. Also, when you are smashing, it is important not to follow the shuttle all the way through, let it disappear forward. If you drop your head, the shot will be too low.
TOP1Fwili-k.transcript: Kind: captions Language: en on behalf of TV lesson.com I'm Dave zaro with usab badminton toorgle on intermediate badminton I'm going to show you how to smash now when your opponent hits a shot up and it's about 2/3 from 2/3 forward in singles you should smash now in doubles you can get away with smashing all the way from the back because you've got a partner covering you but when you do the smash you are going to turn sideways like this you are going to use your torso and you are going to reach up as you reach up your torso is going to come across and you are going to swing across your body and when you do that your racket you will notice is coming across like that so you are putting all of your power into it this is very much like throwing a ball but you're going to be throwing it down so when you smash just like from The Beginner's badon where it's one two three you are going to go one two three and you are going to hit it in front you always make contact in front of you Sean will show you how the smash is done if you'll notice he's making contact in front of him at every time and also when you are smashing it's important for you not to follow the shuttle all the way through when you are smashing if you are really looking at the shuttle you will see it disappear up there when you hit it properly it will go if you drop your head to see where it's going then you're going to drop the whole shot and it will be lower on behalf of tvon.com this is Dave zaro thanks for watching

q6sLCLnTuik.description:

http://www.purdyandpower.co.uk | Appointments: 01580 720990

Are you looking for the perfect pro blowdry?  Even one that you can recreate at home?

Well, welcome to Purdy and Power, the best hairdressers in the middle of the picturesque town of Cranbrook, Kent.

Let Jack, one of the experienced stylists from the Purdy & Power hairdressing team show you how to get a professional blowdry at home.  Or, if you want to get that extra professional look for a special occasion, why not come into our salon and get pampered by our expert stylists?

Jack will show you how to prepare the hair for blowdrying by shampooing and conditioning, towel drying, adding products and rough drying.

He'll then apply three key products to use when you're doing round-brush blow drying: an oil, something that's going to make it sleek and shiny, a heat protector and something that's going to give you lift at the roots. 

Now we're ready to go in with the blow dryer. 

Jack shows you how to section the hair by taking the top section about an inch each side of his client Sam's parting.  He blow dries through this to give it height. Then Jack creates a zig-zag section at the back of the hair. This way, as you're blow drying though it you won't leave a harsh line in the middle. 

So take one section, between an inch and an inch and a half wide depending on the size of the brush that you use and the thickness of the hair. 

Sam's hair is quite thick and Jack's using quite a wide brush. So he's going to take about an inch and a half. It's important when you're doing this to blow dry using lots of tension to pull out any frizz and curl from the hair. Pull the section upwards to get lift at the root. Use the cool setting on your hair dryer once the hair is dry and wrapped about the brush. And gently unravel so as not to brush into it like how we're doing.

Jack continues to do this all the way up Sam's head. 

Now that he's done the back and the sides of the blow dry, Jack always leaves the fringe in the top for last because obviously it sits on the rest of it. 

Jack then blow dries the fringe forward and then all of this hair on top backwards to achieve optimal height, and then obviously once it's all blow dried, you can dress it out like you would a set. 

Just lift the fringe up and smooth it around the brush so you can get a little bit of height, just so that it still sits smoothly. And after you blowdry the crown area, in sections about an inch thick bring the sections forward as slow as you can and put the hair underneath as well and that's what supports the volume that you're putting in the hair.   . 

If you are looking for the best hairdresser in Cranbrook, Kent, give us a call now to make an appointment on 01580 720990.  Or visit our website at http://www.purdyandpower.co.uk

zRBspE-uJUo.title: Swimming Inspired Workouts
zRBspE-uJUo.description: This workout focuses on strength, with the inclusion of plyometrics and total body exercises, such as lunges with overhead press, push-ups with a single leg raise and spider walks. These full body integrated movements translate well to swimming, as the strokes performed in the sport also involve the recruitment of all major muscles.
zRBspE-uJUo.transcript: Kind: captions Language: en [Music] Well, this workout is a swimming inspired workout. Swimming is a great form of exercise. So, whether you're new to heading into the pool or have been a seasoned swimmer, it does provide a great cardiovascular challenge, really help you to build your endurance. Um, it's also low impact. So, it's really accessible for people of all ability levels. Again, whether you're brand new to swimming or you've been swimming for a long period of time. So, all of the workouts do consist of a warm-up, a conditioning phase, which is the main part of the workout, and then also a cool down. We started with a warm-up of a 200 meter freestyle. We then followed it with a 100 meters using the kickboard. So, to really focus on ensuring that proper kicking motion, which will be critical to actually executing the freestyle stroke. The main part of the workout consisted of five components and this is where we basically completed the freestyle stroke but we did so at various intensities or speeds. So we did 50 meters at a slow pace six times. We then followed that with freestyle again 50 m six times at a medium pace. We then at the center of our workout focused on a fast pace. This is going to be closer to your race style pace. We did that 50 meters four times and then we basically worked back down that ladder going back to 50 meters freestyle at a medium pace six times and then again 50 meters slow pace six times. It's also really important as I mentioned to ensure efficiency in the pool that we do focus on strength and flexibility outside of the pool. We want to strengthen muscles but we also want to stretch muscles. So some of the things that we showed as part of the cool down we focus on the hip flexors with the supine hip flexor stretch. really easy way to open up that key area of the body. So great if you spend many hours a day sitting at a desk or driving in a car with the hips in a flex position. Great to help open up that area which is important when you head into the pool and start kicking. We also then focus on the upper body. So some great exercises to help stretch out the lat specifically that part of the back. So we did some things like child's pose that works into the spine. So the erector spin that musculature of the low back helping to stretch that area. We also included a lat stretch and we utilized a piece of equipment that's poolside, but that can also be done indoors using anything from a couch or a chair to a raised bench to put your hands on. So, what we've showed today are some swimming specific drills. So, things you'll actually be doing in the pool. And what you saw is actually just a variation on different tempos. So, really the focus is an endurancebased workout. And you can certainly take it at your own pace. Those total body integrated exercise involve all those key muscle groups. So, a great way to get a great workout in a short amount of time. [Music]

Here I show you how to shovel snow fast and do it the right way.
The best way to clean your driveway after a snowstorm and how to do it in three simple steps.  
1. Make one pass down the middle of your driveway first.  
2. Then you want to push the snow to one side 
3 And push the snow to the other side in quick, easy sweeps.
The best way to shovel snow efficiently is to get into a rhythm. 
It keeps up your momentum and helps you to move along without pausing and allowing you to slow up. 
I can shovel my drive quicker than it takes for some of my neighbors to start up their blowers and walk slowly behind blowing snow everywhere. So often I see them have to stop and adjust the chute , so that they don't blow snow on their neighbors  drive or lawn or  make sure that they are not blowing it back behind him or in front of them. Which makes no sense at all. 
Shoveling snow from my drive is quiet,  is 100% green, and I bring my heart rate up to about 100 bpm burning calories in the process. not bad!!

enASD1KDX24.title: Pumping While Raking Leaves (Breastfeeding Tutorial)
enASD1KDX24.description:
Jen from Life With Levi shows you how to pump breast milk while raking leaves with a PumpEase hands-free pumping bra.

---------------

Backstory: Shortly after my son was born, I had to have surgery on my right breast. While recovering, it was impossible to nurse him the traditional way, but I didn't want to give up breastfeeding altogether. Instead, I turned to exclusive pumping. 

If you've never pumped before, let me tell you, it's a lot of work. To maintain my breast milk supply, I kept the same pumping schedule as his feeding schedule, including getting up in the middle of the night, pumping during breaks at work, and pumping between the college classes I was taking at night. 

Once I learned about the magic of a hands-free pumping bra, I decided to have some fun with it and see how many "normal" activities I could do while still pumping. Yes, the setup takes time, but it was nice to not have to stop and drop everything multiple times a day to pump. 

View the playlist for all of my "pumping while" videos: https://bit.ly/pumping-playlist

puPMvwv2kmg.title: Topless Step Down Under by Min Lomo, Stephen Parker, and Ryan Hogan
puPMvwv2kmg.description:
Preview of Topless Step Down Under by Min Lomo, Stephen Parker, and Ryan Hogan.  Full DVD available at Fitness Organica, http://www.fitnessorganica.com/products/ToplessStepDownUnder.html

Is Australia a breeding ground for the most talented, creative, and logical fitness presenters in the world? I'm beginning to think so! From the continent that gave us Marcus Irwin and Rebecca Small, now we have Min Lomo, Stephen Parker, and Ryan Hogan. Following the same teaching principles that put Marcus and Rebecca on the map, while adding their own style and personality, this talented trio takes you through a 62-minute step workout. No, they're not topless -- topless step means that the combinations are not repeated. Each of the three builds a combination from the bottom up, and then you move on to another. 

Stephen Parker starts out with a warmup to get you ready for what's to come. 

Min Lomo takes over with combination #1. With his spot-on cueing and expert layering, he'll have you traveling and turning all around the step even if you thought you couldn't. 

Next up is Stephen Parker. He steadily adds impact and propulsion to his combo, making the final product a real intensity blast. 

Ryan Hogan teaches the third combo. He takes you on a ride to all sides of the step with directional and rhythm variations. Ryan also leads the well-deserved cooldown and stretch. 

The DVD chapter options give you a choice of doing the entire step workout at once or going directly to the combination you want.

EGrXaq213Oc.title: Teaching Kids to Snowboard: The Mini-Shred Movement!
EGrXaq213Oc.description:
Burton Snowboards and Mint Snowboard School present The Mini-Shred Movement; proving that you are never too young, or too cute, to snowboard! They give a professional and educational take on snowboarding for 3-6 year old kids. 

“Kids can’t snowboard until they are 7 years old, right?”
WRONG! 

The perceived idea that kids are not able to snowboard until age 7, due to build and physique, is being proven wrong. As soon as kids can stand they can snowboard. Jumps, rails and even simple turns can wait, but they can still enjoy the sensation of sliding on snow from a very early age. 

Top, professional instruction will make this early stage fun and exciting with learning hidden in games. Mint Snowboard School have built up a comprehensive program of fun-focused teaching and innovative games… it’s all about learning through play.

Burton Snowboards have helped drive this new generation of mini-shredders, making huge steps forwards in equipment adapted to little people. Along with developments in boards, boots & bindings, there’s also the Riglet reel, a Burton creation that is key for teaching the real ankle-biters!

------------------------------------------
http://www.mintsnowboarding.com
http://www.learntosnowboard.com
------------------------------------------

Established in 2005, Mint Snowboard School provides top-level snowboard instruction and coaching in the Portes du Soleil resorts of Morzine, Avoriaz, Les Gets and Chatel in France. Mint is a Burton Learn to Ride centre and its instructors offer easy to understand techniques and fun-focused snowboard coaching for all ages and levels.

Check out our specialised Mini-Shred lessons & holidays in Morzine, France: http://bit.ly/1nwPv0x

Zc8zn0sKfwo.title: Tomato And Cheese Pasta Bake: Food Fest 3
Zc8zn0sKfwo.description:
In this episode of Food Fest, chef Jonny Marsh shows you how to make a classic tomato and cheese pasta bake. Your friends will love it!

Subscribe! http://www.youtube.com/subscription_center?add_user=thetastytenner
Check Out Our Channel Page: http://www.youtube.com/user/thetastytenner
Like Us On Facebook! https://www.facebook.com/TheTastyTenner
Follow Us On Twitter! https://twitter.com/TheTastyTenner

Ingredients:

300 g dried penne pasta
Olive oil
1 onion, chopped finely
1 garlic clove, crushed
3-4 sprigs of fresh thyme
5 slices of bacon, cut into chunks
1 tsp crushed chillies
400 g tinned tomatoes
1 1/2 tsp caster sugar
1 tbsp finely chopped fresh parsley
2 large handfuls of grated cheddar
Salt
Pepper

Step 1: Cook Your Pasta
Preheat your oven to  200°c. Bring a pan of salted water to the boil and add your pasta. Cook to the instructions on the packet, and then drain. Return your pasta to the pan.

Step 2: Make The Tomato Sauce
Heat some oil in a large frying pan. Add you chopped onion, garlic and thyme to the pan, along with your sliced bacon. Move the ingredients around the pan to ensure they cook evenly. Once the bacon begins to crisp up, sprinkle over some crushed chillies and pour in your tinned tomatoes. Give everything a good mix. Season with salt and pepper and sprinkle in one-and-a-half teaspoons of sugar. While the sauce is simmering, finely chop up your parsley and add it to your pan. Leave to simmer for another 3-4 minutes.

Step 3: Combine The Sauce And Pasta
Pour your tomato sauce over your drained pasta and mix well to ensure all the pasta gets coated. Pour the mixture into your dish and then top with grated cheese. Cook for 10-15 minutes until all of the cheese has melted and has begun to turn golden brown. Serve on its own or with a side salad.

A powerbomb is a professional wrestling throw in which an opponent is lifted (usually so that they are sitting on the wrestler's shoulders) and then slammed back-first down to the mat.[1] The standard powerbomb sees an opponent first placed in a standing headscissors position (bent forward with their head placed between the attacking wrestler's thighs). He is then lifted on the wrestler's shoulders and slammed down back-first to the mat.[1] A prawn hold is commonly used for a pinning powerbomb.

Powerbombs are sometimes used in mixed martial arts competitions, when a fighter attempts to slam another fighter who has him trapped in a triangle choke. In professional wrestling, it is also sometimes used by a bigger wrestler as a counter to an attempted hurricanrana by a smaller wrestler. While it was associated with super-heavyweight wrestlers, the move was innovated by Lou Thesz[2]

Knife sharpening lessons in the office. No back stabbing allowed!. Another team training initiative by Food Strategy. The foodservice design team at www.FoodStrategy.com.au are more than specialist designers. They have in-depth training in many facets of the food industry from sharpening knives to heating the pans with chefs. This video includes full instructions at the end on how to use a steel to sharpen your knives. LOCAL PEOPLE | GLOBAL VISION
Once you have had an edge put on your knives it is now very important to maintain that edge and keep it better than new, so this is where a sharpening steel come into play.Contrary to popular belief, a sharpening steel does not sharpen a knife. The purpose of a steel is to hone the edge of the knife. Through regular use, the edge of a knife will begin to lose its original sharpness, by creating a fine burr, which is when the knifes edge rolls over and becomes dull. The sharpening steel will straighten the edge and remove this burr. Eventually though, the steel will only do this so many times and your knife will become blunt and need to be sharpened again by A Wicked Edge Sharpening.

_MWyhJS4KbM.title: Window Cleaning World Record Holder Terry Burrows
_MWyhJS4KbM.description:
http://robinson-solutions.blogspot.com/2009/10/brodex-systems-at-fwc-show-squeegee.html
Fastest window cleaner-world record set by Terrry "Turbo" Burrows in BLACKPOOL, Lancashire, UK. Martial Arts specialist, Terry Burrows, aka "Turbo Terry", 54, cleaned cleaned three 4ft (1.2m) high windows in just 9.14 seconds at the 2009 window cleaning competition-setting the new world record for the Fastest window cleaner. Terry actually finished the windows in a super-speedy 8.14 seconds, but got a one-second time penalty as he left two water marks on the glass. Terry 'Turbo' Burrows, from Essex, has a black belt in karate and he has been cleaning windows for 30 years said his success was due "to moving the body in sequence". "I clean the windows in just 16 moves, and it's pretty intense," he said. Terry was in the resort for the Federation of Window Cleaners annual conference and decided to try to better his existing 9.24 second time. You might think that is pretty fast for cleaning a window that measures 45 inches square including wiping the window sill.  But, what makes Terry's record incredible is that the strict competition rules state that he must clean three windows, each measuring 45 inches square, and wipe the sill!  There are time penalties deducted for any water marks left on the glass and the competitor is limited to a maximum squeegee size of 12 inches. Terry Burrows said: "I'm elated to have shaved so much time off my record. "It's extremely hard, it takes a while to warm up and I drove 270 miles this morning so I wasn't feeling too fresh. By my fourth time, however, I was back in the zone and actually managed to clean the planes in 8.14 seconds with two half-second time penalties." He smashed his first record in 1995 as part of TV show Record Breakers with a speed of 9.99 seconds. 
In 2005 he broke his own Guinness world record for the Fastest window cleaner during The Cleaning Show at NEC Birmingham with a 9.24 second time. 
Terry 'Turbo' Burrows said: "I'd never say never as far as beating my own record again goes, but at the end of the day, a man can only go so fast. "I would love to die with my world record and know I went as the world's fastest window cleaner."

FmaW2KK4wWU.transcript: Kind: captions Language: en the home serve guide to Hanging wallpaper wallpaper is a great way of brightening up your room but it's a messy job if you don't know what you are doing before you start watch how to prepare your wall for wallpapering depending on the size of the wall you are papering it shouldn't take you more than a few hours to do if you feel up to the job home serve is here to show you how to do it step one gear to do a good job you'll need scissors a tape measure a large soft wall brush a fold up pasting table or WIP clean table a bucket a plum line a pencil a paper hanging brush and wallpaper paste this is usually sold as powder or flakes for mixing but to save time and hassle you can buite Ready Mixed step two measure and cut the wallpaper carefully measure the length required which is normally the height of the wall and cut from the roll make sure that you allow an extra 50 mm at both the top and bottom for final trimming always make sure that the pattern is the right way up and never ever assume that the outside of the Roll is the top this could lead to all sorts of trouble and hilarity from others before cutting the next lengths ensure that the pattern matches up with previous ones top tip after you've cut it Mark the back of the paper with a T at the top this will avoid any confusion later on step three Plum spirit level the last thing you want is wonky wallpaper so Mark a vertical pencil line against a plum line or spirit level the plum line should be about 25 mm less than the width of the roll away from the starting point so you end up papering over it and there's no chance of it being seen through the seam later on step four pasting now you get to the messy bit spread a length of wallpaper face down on the table and start to brush the paste down the length and out towards the edges don't pull the brush back across the edge of the paper as it will leave paste on the front of the paper if you do manage to get paste on the front Don't Panic just dab it off with a wet sponge step five soaking once pasted fold the paper inwards bottom to middle and top to Middle then put the paper to one side to soak check the instructions to see how long it needs to be soaked for don't try and skip this steps to save time as by allowing it to soak it minimizes blisters on the Hong wall paper step six hang once the paper has soaked pick up the top of the paper and lightly stick the top half of the length to the wall allowing the 50 mm for trimming Slide the paper into position smooth down the middle with a paper hangers brush and then work out towards the edge removing air bubbles as you go step seven trim take the scissors and carefully run the back of them along the angle of the ceiling and the top of the wall and the skirting at the bottom gently pull the paper away from the wall and trim the excess then brush back into place so it looks nice and neat step eight tidy now all you need to do is tidy it up and make sure it looks like a professional has done it wipe the surpless paste from the surface of the paper and the ceiling and the skirting with a damp sponge so that is your first length of wallpaper done keep following the steps until you have completed the room and your home looks fantastic another job well done

yfjnahzAPSc.title: The Sport of Cricket: How to Play, Rules
yfjnahzAPSc.transcript: Kind: captions Language: en Cricket essentially boils down to this. You see a ball, you hit a ball. [Music] One of the the common uh conceptions is that cricket is a sport that lasts 5 days. And while that's true and I'd love to stop working for 5 days, it's only the top 10 teams in the world that play for 5 days. For the rest of the world, for club cricket, generally it's a game played over six to eight hours. You have 11 players aside. The objective is to score more points than the other team. So you have two innings, one per team. One team smashes maybe 200, 300 runs. Other team tries to chase it down. [Music] Playing surface is very important to cricket. So here obviously the grass is long but in a proper cricket field the grass has got to be maximum one inch long because you're trying to hit the ball along the ground. The moment it's over an inch you're struggling if you're a beginner, you're struggling if you're a kid. The center of the pitch is the most important. We have a strip which is 66 ft or 22 yd long. That is where the ball bounces before it reaches the batsman. It has to be like a road. It has to be very compacted. That's called the wicket. Now to make this really confusing for viewers, the yellow sticks you see are also called the wickets. If you get a batsman out, that is also called the wicket. There's only one word to learn. It can't be that hard. Cricket is broken down into sets which are called overs. And an over is six balls bowled in one direction by the bowler. At the end of that, the field turns around and another bowler bowl six balls in the other direction. Everybody on the team can bowl, right? So, it doesn't just have to be one pitcher like in baseball. But unlike baseball, you don't have to just hit it in the sort of triangle. In cricket, you can play 360°. The way you score runs is by exchanging with the other batsman. That's one run. So, you have two batsmen standing at all times. And the ways to get out, if you hit the ball in the air and somebody catches it, you're out. Even if you get the slightest touch of the bat on the ball and the wicket keeper catches it behind, you're out. If it touches your glove, you're out. If you hit the ball and as you're running, someone gets the ball and throws it and knocks over the wicket, you're out. You can be out by being bowled out, which is when the bowler bowls the ball, you miss it, and it goes through and knocks down the wicket. Another way to be out, which is more uh technical, is called LBW, which is leg before wicket. Basically, that means you're not allowed to stop the ball from hitting the wicket with your body. If the umpire decides that the way the ball was going would have hit the wicket if the batsman hadn't stopped it with his body, the batsman's out. Oh, I remembered another way of being out. Uh, you can be what's called stumped. You've got a crease on the ground. You always have to have one foot either on or behind that crease. If the ball comes towards you and you step forward from your crease to try to hit the ball and miss the ball, the wicket keeper can catch the ball and knock the wicket off before you put your foot behind the crease. It's like being run out. [Music]

x18x9BKMAlk.transcript: Kind: captions Language: en He's considered the founder of Tai Chi Chuen or Tai Chi boxing, an internal martial arts style. Tang, the man himself was claimed to have written that in every movement, every part of the body must be light, agile and connected in a sequence. The postures continuous, the movement rooted in the feet, released through the legs, focused on the waist and expressed with the fingers. One story has it that Chang saw a bird of prey attacking a snake. He noticed how the snake defended itself by keeping still and alert before counterattacking and killing the bird. With his knowledge of dowoism and shaoling kung fu, an external or hard fighting style, Chang was inspired to create a new martial art based on softness and yielding. Many details of Chang's life remain unclear. Much of what has been written about him varies according to different sources. Chang was a legendary Chinese Dowist priest believed to have lived for about 200 years. Although the date of his death is unclear, it is said he lived from 1247 to 1447 AD. If this were the case, then Chang would have lived during the Song, Yuen, and Ming dynasties. According to one tradition, Chang was born near Lung Hu Shan or Dragon Tiger Mountain in southeast China's Chiang province. This is one of the four sacred mountains of Daoism. One story has it that Chang had a childhood illness and lost his eyesight. His father took him to the nearby Dowi temple and within a week Chang regained his eyesight. The Dowi priest then took Jang as a disciple and taught him writing and martial arts. Chang's father hoped that his son would sit for the state examination for a career in the government. But Chang was not interested. He had no interest in fame or wealth. It was said that Chang turned down an official position, gave away his property to his family, and then traveled around China. He went to live at Mount Hua before settling at Wuang Mountains, where there are many Dowi monasteries. Two Ming Dynasty emperors each ordered a huge stone tablet erected on Wuang Mountains to honor Tang as a Dawi saint. Chang is believed to be a sien a dowi term for an immortal or an enlightened person. Chang's boxing art was passed down through the generations, most notably in a Chan village where it evolved into the Chan style of Tai Chi. Other martial artists who learned from the masters in a Chan village then created their own systems and the art split into five family systems. Chen, Yang, Wu, Sunun, and Hao. These styles, plus a variety of modern styles, are now practiced by millions around the world. Yet, the original movements and theories of Chung's boxing art are now lost.

Zkz4ef53YjA.description:
Harold McGee, author of Keys to Good Cooking: A Guide to Making the Best of Foods and Recipes, shares a handy way to speed your pasta dinner along. Plus it's ecofriendly!

======================CHOW.com=========================
CHOW Tips are the shared wisdom of our community. If you've figured out some piece of food, drink, or cooking wisdom that the world has to know about, send us a message and tell us what you've got in mind!

See all the newest uploads from CHOW with the Latest Videos playlist: http://bit.ly/owLvNO

Subscribe to CHOW: http://bit.ly/xTzxYj

For more recipes, stories and videos, check out http://www.chow.com/videos
CHOW on Twitter: http://twitter.com/#!/CHOW
CHOW on Facebook: http://www.facebook.com/Chow
========================================================

TRANSCRIPT
Most traditional recipes for making pasta tell you to start out with lots and lots of water and heat it up to the boil before you add the pasta.  Turns out that you don't need to do that.  You can save a lot of time, a lot of water, a lot of energy by starting out with cold water and a frying pan.  Put the pasta in the frying pan.  Pour a quart and a half or so of water on top of the pasta.  Turn on the heat and, because the pasta is cold, the pasta won't stick to itself at the very beginning.  When it's done you have pasta that's perfectly cooked and you have a thickened liquid that you can use to make all kinds of sauces.

ux_qqONPSrc.title: Vegetable and Chef Salad
ux_qqONPSrc.description: Make your own basic vegetable salad and then transform it into a chef salad with a just a few more ingredients.
ux_qqONPSrc.transcript: Kind: captions Language: en Welcome to startcooking.com. Hi, my name is Kathy Maester. Today I'm going to show you how to make a vegetable salad. Then we're going to add a few extras and turn it into a fabulous chef salad. So go grab a knife, a cutting board, a vegetable peeler, a salad bowl, and we'll be ready to start cooking. The basic ingredients I'm using today are lettuce, a red pepper, two stalks of celery, some cherry tomatoes, some green onion, a cucumber, and two carrots. The first step is to wash the vegetables we're going to be using. We also need to peel the carrots and the cucumbers. Remember, always peel away from your body, no matter what you're peeling. Now, I'm going to chop the lettuce into bite-sized pieces. The red pepper is first cut in half, then the stem and the seeds are removed. Now cut it into strips and then it gets coarsely chopped. I have three different types of cucumbers. This little one is called a pickling cucumber. This one is called an English cucumber. This is just a regular cucumber. They all taste pretty much the same and they add a nice crunch to the salad. I think I'll add the pickling cube to my salad. Next, we're going to slice two carrots and add them to our salad. We need to trim off the ends of the celery. Then slice the celery into about 1/4 in slices. Now for the tomatoes. I love cherry tomatoes. Be sure to cut them in half or they tend to go flying across the room when you try to stab them with your fork. Green onions are great on salads. The green part has a very mild flavor and the white part gets much stronger. Trim off the ends, then cut them into about 3-in strips. Cut them together and start slicing. Add the dressing just before you serve your salad. If we want to turn this into a chef salad, just add some extras like chicken, ham, eggs, kidney beans, cheese, bacon bits, even some leftover boiled potatoes. That's what's great about a chef salad. You can toss in whatever you like, add some dressing, and you've got yourself a meal. Enjoy.

Here is how to fix sqeaky bicycle brakes on your bike. If your bike squeaks when you stop, and it has rubber rim-pad brakes, here's how to stop the squeaking noise from happening.  Squeaky brakes are easy to fix.  To quiet squeaky bike brakes, first wash the rim and brake pads with something that isn't oily. Try plain water or rubbing alcohol.  If your bicycle brakes keep squeaking and making noise, try sanding down the brake pads a little bit with sandpaper, and then clean the bicycle brake pads to remove any sand from the sand paper.  This should quiet your squeaky bicycle brakes.  If your bike's brake still make a squeaking noise, try new brake pads.  If new brake pads don't stop the squeaking, try rubbing the rim with steel wool to smooth it out.  This is how to quiet squeaky bicycle brakes.

7RDn5qTQquE.title: Strength of the shot - Squash tips #11 How to increase the speed and strength of your racket swing
7RDn5qTQquE.description:
Learn all of squash fundamentals, free e-book: http://goo.gl/d83Ak5
Related Article: http://adf.ly/ThoKO

Song by Atron. Check his channel here: http://www.youtube.com/user/TheOfficialAtron

The three key concept taught in this video are:

-Open soon and high over your shoulder
Preparing the shot as soon as you realize where the ball is going will grant you the chance to decide whether you want to forestall the shot or not, also you will get more power thanks to gravity.

-Stay away from the ball
By staying far away from the ball and extending yourself you will have more momentum and throw a faster ball, you will also have a major tactical advantage by being able to control the center more often

-Create a stable base
If you make a oblique step when going for the ball and then bend your knees you will be able to transfer your body weight and momentum into your shot enhancing it.

If you want some practical exercise to work on these skills check out: http://www.squash-tips.com

Daily tips @ www.twitter.com/squash_tips

qhnWJ4G5JMA.transcript: Kind: captions Language: en Hi, I'm Katherine. I'm a personal trainer at the Upper Valley Aquatic Center and I'm also a certified spitting instructor. I'm going to show you how to properly seat yourself on a spinning bike. So, whether or not you've been on the bike before, you're going to want to be properly seated. The first step is to make sure that your seat height is proper. So, what you're going to do is you're going to unscrew this knob at the bottom. This is located on the back of the bike. You're going to pull the knob out as it's undone being screwed. I know already my height is F. And I'll show you why I know that. Now that I'm on letter F, I'm then going to check the position of the top of my hipbone with the seat. And I can see now that the size matches my hip. So with that, I can lift my leg up. And it shows also that my leg is parallel with the seat. Your next step is to move the seat laterally. So it'll change your position with the bike seat with the handlebars. So what you're going to do is unscrew this knob located right underneath the seat. I already know that I'm a four and a half. And you can see that the arrow shows where you are. And I'm going to explain why I know that. So, what you're going to do is screw this back on nice and tight. Before you hop on the bike, just make sure everything's settled in. You don't want to jump on when things aren't all the way screwed in. So, now you can hop on the bike. The next step is to figure out where if the seat position is correct. The reason why I know that is because when I come down, I've got a nice 35 to 25 degree angle with my legs. My hips don't exactly move a lot and I'm also not reaching with my legs. So, if I'm on here comfortably, I don't have to move anything out of the norm and my legs move. Some of the biggest pointers is to put your feet starting at 9090. right here. I can see down that my shoelace is the first shoelace is showing from my knee. The other pointer is when you're in another position this way. Um you can do the same thing with this leg. Okay. So, the next step is to figure out which height for the handlebars is right for you. Um my biggest advice would be if you're a beginner, you're going to want to have your your handlebar height a little bit higher. This is because most advanced riders provide a lot lower. If you're new to this um sport, you're going to want to make sure that you're more upright. This way, it doesn't put any tension on your back. So, right now, my handlebars are on a nine. And I think that that's a great start to do. So, if you would like to change the handlebars, it's going to be the same uh hander handle as the seat one. r5mwKEhEsHA.title: How To Put Contacts In:]
r5mwKEhEsHA.description:
Here's a step by step description on how to put contacts in:
1-Wash your hands with soap and water!!! This is THE MOST important step!

2-Get your contact out of the case and put it on your finger.[I use my pointer finger. You may find it easer to use your ring finger or middle finger.]

3-I, personally, put my contact on my left finger, dry my right finger, then put the contact back on my right finger.[It makes it a lot easier for the contact to stick to my eye.]

4-Using the hand with your contact on it, pull your eye down. Using your other hand, pull the eyelid up.

5-Then, place your contact in your eye, and while STILL holding it there, look up-down-left-right, then take your finger off of your contact.

6-BEFORE you close your eye, repeat looking up-down-left-right to remove any bubbles from under your contant.

7-Repeat the process with the other eye:]
r5mwKEhEsHA.transcript: Kind: captions Language: en Hey YouTubers, this is going to be a video tutorial on how to put contacts in. The first thing you're going to do is wash your hands. That is one of the most important things that you need to do because your hands are so dirty and disgusting. Like when you walk around all day, you're like touching things and that your hands can like have a lot of bacteria and stuff and you don't want to put that in your eye. So, you're going to wash your hands with soap and water. And then you want to dry them. Uh, then what you do is you take your contact holder, contact case, and you should have had your contact in the contact lens cleaner overnight just for a good amount of time to disinfect it. And then you're going to get your contact, which is probably one of the hardest things sometimes. Um, okay. Then what I personally find helps me a lot is if my I use my right finger to put it in, but by using my finger to take my contact out, it's like really wet and it's harder for the contact to stick in my eye. So, I'm going to use the same washcloth and dry off my finger while my contact is resting on my left hand. Then I'm going to slip it over and then pull my eye down with this finger. Pull it up with the other finger and then slowly put it in. Now, this may take a few attempts because it is really hard to do sometimes. So then when you think you have it in, you're going to look to the left, to the right, up and down. Then when it's in, you're going to look up and down, to the left and to the right. And then just like look all around because there might be a little air bubble in there and you want to get it out. Then you close your eyes and it's in. There you go.

OAot8XBeLrs.title: Gols, Floripa 4 x 1 Corinthians - Liga Futsal 10/08/2014
OAot8XBeLrs.description:
Curtam nossa página: http://www.facebook.com/LeandroSportsVideos

Corinthians não resiste ao Floripa e perde a invencibilidade na Liga Futsal
Jogando fora de casa, Timão é derrotado por 4 a 1 e conhece o seu primeiro revés na competição. Jaraguá bate Assoeva e abre cinco pontos na liderança. Brigando ponto a ponto com o Jaraguá pela liderança deste início de Liga Futsal, o Corinthians sofreu grande revés neste sábado, em Florianópolis. Não bastasse a vitória por 6 a 3 do concorrente sobre a Assoeva, fora de casa, também neste sábado, o Timão perdeu por 4 a 1 para o Floripa, que balançou a rede com Renatinho (dois), Antônio e Guto, com Alex fazendo o de honra do Alvinegro do Parque São Jorge. O Corinthians está em segundo na classificação (empatado com Blumenau e com o próprio Floripa), com 14 pontos, atrás do Jaraguá, que abriu cinco pontos de frente. O Timão descansa na rodada desta segunda-feira, enquanto o Jaraguá pega o Carlos Barbosa às 19h15, em Carlos Barbosa (RS), com transmissão ao vivo do SporTV.
O jogo começou movimentado. Aos dois minutos, Vini arrancou sozinho em contra-ataque e foi derrubado por Deivd. O árbitro confirmou a falta, mas advertiu o goleiro corintiano apenas com o cartão amarelo. A resposta do Corinthians veio em finalização frontal de Simi, no minuto seguinte. Bem colocado, Carlos fez a defesa. Aos seis, Vini recebeu na direita do ataque do Floripa, dominou e mandou uma bomba. Deivd conseguiu defender com dificuldade, chegando a deslocar a trave. O Timão voltou a assustar aos oito. Depois de receber passe na entrada da área, Simi tentou concluir de calcanhar, mas Carlos pegou. Aos 12, foi a vez de Neguinho colocar o goleiro do Floripa para trabalhar, dessa vez em chute frontal da entrada da área. Segundos depois, o veterano Betão disparou em petardo da esquerda do ataque corintiano, e lá estava Carlos para salvar o time da casa novamente.
Apesar do melhor momento do rival, foi o Florianópolis quem saiu na frente aos 15. Após passe de Renatinho, Vini dominou na frente e tocou na saída de Deivd. A bola pegou na trave e sobrou para Antônio empurrar para as redes. O gol não abateu o Corinthians, que continuou pressionando. Aos 17, Fernando arriscou de longe, e Carlos espalmou pela lateral. Nos segundos finais, Schumacher ainda teve liberdade para finalizar da direita do ataque, porém, mais uma vez, o goleiro do Floripa apareceu para garantir o resultado parcial.
Blitz corintiana prossegue no segundo tempo
O segundo tempo começou com o mesmo panorama. Retraído, o time catarinense esperava o Corinthians em sua quadra. Aos dois minutos, Leandro avançou pela ala-direita e quase empatou a partida. De tanto insistir, o Timão enfim conseguiu igualar o marcador aos quatro. Após passe de Schumacher, Alex chutou de pé trocado acertando o canto direito de Carlos. Com o gol sofrido, o Florianópolis voltou a sair mais para o jogo. Aos cinco, Deivd fez duas defesas em sequência, uma em finalização de Guto, outra em conclusão de Erverson.
Dois minutos depois, foi a vez de Bynho assustar a defesa corintiana com um tiro rente à trave. Empurrado pela sua torcida, o Floripa continuou crescendo no jogo, e, aos 10, Renatinho recebeu passe na área corintiana, sendo interceptado por Deivd quando ia mandar a bola na rede. Os paulistas só voltaram a chegar com perigo aos 11, em cobrança de falta de Douglinhas. Bem colocado, Carlos jogou a bola pela lateral. No lance seguinte, Betão teve mais uma chance, mas o veterano errou a conclusão de frente para a meta.
A cinco minutos do fim, Fernando recebeu o segundo amarelo ao cometer falta em Erverson e acabou expulso, deixando o Corinthians com um jogador a menos por dois minutos. O Florianópolis tratou de aproveitar a vantagem numérica logo na cobrança da falta que gerou a expulsão. O autor do gol foi Renatinho, em batida que contou com desvio: 2 a 1. O Corinthians mal teve tempo de respirar. Logo após a saída de bola, Guto viu Deivd adiantado e chutou de longe para marcar o terceiro.
O técnico corintiano Lucas Chioro ainda arriscou tudo lançando Leandro como goleiro-linha nos minutos finais, mas já era tarde. Para piorar, Renatinho ainda fez o quarto, fechando o caixão da equipe do Parque São Jorge. Era o fim da invencibilidade de um dos times que mais investiu para a temporada.
Escalações:
Florianópolis: Carlos, Antônio, Jedson, Renatinho e Vini. Entraram: Pedro, Guto, Luizinho, Bynho, Ney, Andrei, Márcio, Roni e Erverson. Técnico: João Carlos Barbosa.
Corinthians: Deivd, Schumacher, Leandro, Alex e Simi. Entraram: Neguinho, Douglas, Bruno, Betão, Joãozinho, Charuto, Fernando e Douglinhas. Técnico: Lucas Chioro.

Know Your Sport is a series of videos giving brief factoids about the Sports Played in Olympics -- Lawn Tennis

Some interesting facts about Tennis 

1. In Tennis, a set consists of games, and games, in turn, consist of points.
2. There are five types of court surface used in professional play: Hard, Clay, Grass, Carpet, Wood
3. A volley is a shot returned to the opponent in mid-air before the ball bounces
4. A winning serve that is not touched by the opponent is called an "ace"
5.  A "love" set means that the loser of the set won zero games, 
6. The chair umpire announces the end of the match with the well-known phrase "Game, set, match" 
7. The longest tennis match lasted 11 hours, 5 minutes in 2010.

-nlAKyoyIuU.title: 白鵬 が33回目の優勝 | Yokozuna Hakuho Makes Sumo History: Wins Record 33rd Tournament Championship
-nlAKyoyIuU.description:
January 23, 2015 JST

Today Yokozuna Hakuhō Shō (real name Mönkhbatyn Davaajargal), a sumo wrestler from Mongolia became the record holder for most tournament championships winning his 33rd crown today and hence breaking the 44 year record held by the legendary Yokozuna Taihō.

Winning one tournament is considered a difficult challenge but to win 33 is quite remarkable. And he did so in a shorter time period than the previous record holder, Yokozuna Taihō Kōki (real name Kōki Naya), with 32 tournament wins in his 11 years.  He also took the record on day 13th of this tournament and still has two more days of matches left.  He could lose the next two matches and still be crowned the winner.

In today's match with long time rival Ozeki Kisenosato, Yokozuna Hakuho actually needed an additional bout because the first one was ruled a draw.  The second bout then was very convincing and made no mistake who the dominant sumo wrestler of all time is.  It was wonderful to personally witness a once-in-a-generation historic event. Congratulations Yokozuna!

Visit my blog for more great insight about Japan, Hawaii and everything in between.

vS0ppdYTwTc.description: Some great tips on French Braiding and working with fine hair.
vS0ppdYTwTc.transcript: Kind: captions Language: en [Music] Today on Tammy's Tips, I'm going to help you learn to French braid hair. If you can braid hair, you can do a French braid. A lot of times, people struggle with French braiding fine textured hair. I'm going to show you a few simple tricks with that to help you as well. Most hair types you can French braid the hair dry, but with fine textured hair, I like to wet it, then apply gel. When using gel, it's best to lather on both sides of your hands, and then run your fingers throughout the whole head of hair. This will help it hold as you start braiding. The reason why I use the back sides of my fingers is so I get it more evenly distributed through the hair. A fine tooth comb will help pick up all those little stray stragglers, especially with a fine textured hair. When braiding the hair, divide your hair in three even sections. I like doing this with my fingers. Then you take the outsides and bring them into the center. To French braid hair, after you've taken all three strands and brought them to the center, you take hair from the outside of the head and match it to the hair that's getting placed in the center. With fine textured hair, I like to comb through it with water and gel and make sure it lays nicely with the one going to the center. Then you repeat the process on the other side. And the finishing touch is wonderful. With the right tools and a little bit of patience, you can have fabulous hair, too. For more time-saving ideas, visit us on the web at www.fashionclassinstyle.com. And remember, true beauty starts with your smile.

ND9mMyNjm5M.transcript: Kind: captions Language: en welcome to the latest your horse open Clinic care video where expert groom Jenny Ellis shares her step-by-step guide to a thorough winter grooming session start with a rubber curry comb and using a firm pressure working circular movements over your horses more muscular areas this will act as a nice massage and will also loosen skirf from his coat use a lighter touch for bonier areas take a nice flicky brush and use a reasonable amount of pressure to flick all the muck and loose hairs from your horse's coat go with the direction of hair growth and work from head to toe na now take your body brush and work over his coat in circles again but really put some pressure on this brush is much softer so you can go even firm with your Strokes to give him a good massage this will also help lift andrin scarf clip twinter coats can get quite greasy underneath rugs so hot clothing is a great remedy take a bucket of hot water as hot as you can stand and add a couple of drops of washing up Liquid shampoo or dle dip your cloth and fully ring it out then wipe your horse all over brush your horse's legs being careful over the vital structures like his tendons pick his feet out make sure his feet are clean and clear of stones to finish off give your horse a final overall brush so his coat is clean and smooth brush out his Mane and tease out his tail to remove Tangles but try not to break the hairs

I have never had the McCafe Frozen Strawberry Lemonade, but I have had the Fruitista Freeze. Are they similar? Anyway, I love refreshing drinks, especially on a hot summer day. What if I was already prepared at home with all the fixings on said day? I wouldn't even have to leave the house. And all my friends would know just where to come hang out. (My friends are the low maintenance, easy to please types). Coming in at 168 calories compared to McDonalds 200, I would pick my version any day.

Frozen Strawberry Lemonade Recipe

Ingredients:

1 1/2 cup frozen strawberries
Juice of 2 Lemons
1/4 cup fresh orange

Description:

Place the frozen strawberries in a glass.

Mix the lemon juice and orange juice together in a separate cup. I didn't use fresh orange juice, but as I typed this, I realized how much better that would have been.

Pour the juice over the frozen strawberries and enjoy.

0RIc6mwDRaQ.title: Beautiful Chanson Classic - Best French Flute Music & Harp Instrumental Solos - Playing with Angels
0RIc6mwDRaQ.description:
Chanson et Badinerie by Pierre Camus. Epic French Classic Harp & Flute solo music instrumental performance piece repertoire. As the sun rose from the east, it filled the magnificent Cathedral of the Madeleine with light. We found ourselves "Playing with the Angels", immersed in its rich sound, strikingly beautiful illumination of colors, and surrounded by an Angelic Musical Choir.  Nurture your mind with great thoughts and uplifting music, for you will never go any higher than you think or feel. Jeannine Goeckeritz, Flute and Tamara Oswald, Harp perform Chanson et Badinerie by Pierre Camus from their CD, Chanson: Songs of Light, Peace and Relaxation. To hear more go to: https://www.harpandflute.com  https://www.jeanninegoeckeritz.com

The "Living Musical Art" of Jeannine Goeckeritz and Tamara Oswald has entertained, inspired and brought beauty to audiences around the world. Whether seeking renewal of the spirit, solace from life's demands, or the warm comfort of a lullaby on a sleepless night, the music of the Oswald Goeckeritz Duo can be enjoyed for its rich beauty and treasured for the light, peace and inspiration it gives. Your enjoyment and enrichment will grow with each new listening experience. 

The Oswald Goeckeritz Duo brings together the rich tone and expressive musical style of Jeannine Goeckeritz with the flowing and graceful virtuosity of Tamara Oswald. Their European tour included multiple performances in Switzerland and Germany, and concluded in the Czech Republic, where they performed at the renowned Žofín Palace in Prague.

Experience the rich signature sound of Jeannine Goeckeritz, who has entertained and enriched audiences around the world.  Her inspiring music gives voice to our hopes, joys, trials and triumphs as Jeannine celebrates life through music.  As a performing artist, she has toured throughout the United States and Europe. As a leading crossover musician, she has collaborated with artists and composers from numerous musical backgrounds, giving her a vast performance repertoire of musical genres.  She has performed under the baton of John Williams at the Winter Olympics and in numerous orchestral productions for headline performers such as Josh Groban, Sarah Brightman, and Andrea Bocelli. Her expressive style breathes life into music that reaches into your heart, creates a musical connection, and takes you on an unforgettable journey that will captivate, entertain and inspire you from beginning to end.

She is one of the most televised flutists and can be seen and heard on the weekly international television and radio broadcast of Music and the Spoken Word,  which has connected her to the hearts and spirit of people throughout the world. Jeannine’s distinctive sound can also be heard on movie soundtracks, television broadcasts, broadway musical theater scores, commercials, video games, numerous recording artists’ CDs, and her YouTube channel.   

Tamara Oswald has performed with the Zurich Tonhalle Orchestra under the direction of such renowned musicians as Christoph Eschenbach and M. Rstropovich, and as a soloist with the Tuttlingen Jugend Orchestra in Germany. Nationally, she has performed with the Pasadena, Long Beach and the Honolulu Symphonies, and as a soloist with the Santa Monica Symphony, the University of Southern California, University of Utah, the Orchestra at Temple Square, Utah Chamber Artists and the Utah Symphony. She has been the recipient of esteemed musical awards from the American Harp Society and has competed as a semi-finalist at both the Israeli and Rome International Harp competitions.

Jeannine Goeckeritz and Tamara Oswald are principal flute and principal harp with the Orchestra at Temple Square where they perform, record and tour with the Tabernacle Choir at Temple Square.  They have performed at venues such as Berlin Philharmonie, Musikverein, Bozar Centre For Fine Arts, Carnegie Hall, Lincoln Center, Ravinia, Disney Hall, Wolftrap, Chautauqua, Red Rocks, and the historic Salt Lake Tabernacle. Performances include the weekly international broadcast of Music and the Spoken Word and the annual PBS Christmas Specials of the Tabernacle Choir and Orchestra at Temple Square with featured headline artists such as Alfie Boe, Natalie Cole, Sissel, The King's Singers, Renée Fleming, Bryn Terfel, Frederica Von Stada, Brian Stokes Mitchell, Kristin Chenoweth and Sesame Street Muppets.
https://www.thetabernaclechoir.org/

RgMAHuMVRcU.title: How to prune a mango tree (engl)
RgMAHuMVRcU.description: Explains the principles of maintenance pruning of mango trees. Pictures taken on mango farms in Brong Ahafo Region.
RgMAHuMVRcU.transcript: Kind: captions Language: en Welcome to this agric tutorial. In this edition, we will show you how to prune a mango tree. In pruning, we selectively remove unproductive shoots and branches to improve the health of the tree and control its growth. Some of the major reasons why you should practice pruning are the following. One, to admit light and air into the canopies of your trees. Two, to enhance flowering in a way that you can produce high quality mangoes which meet international export standards. Three, improve effective control of pest and diseases. There are two types of pruning. One formative pruning which is carried out on young trees and two maintenance pruning which is continuously done every year after the harvest. Here you see Mr. Fon welldressed for the pruning exercise. He wears a plastic helmet, gloves, Wellington boots, and a protective coat. For pruning, you need the following tools. One, hand shares. Two, long shares. Three, a pruning saw. And four, a pruning pole. Here you can see an example of a well pruned mango tree. The branches are evenly distributed, and there are no branches growing into the center of the canopy. This is a tree that has not been pruned. You can see it has a dense canopy with branches growing in all directions. It is very difficult to produce mangoes of high quality with such a tree. In pruning, it is very important to know where you have to cut the branches. We are looking for branches with a V or an A shape. All branches which have not developed either the V or the A shape should be cut off. In the image, you can see a yellow line indicating branches to be removed. We now show you how best to cut your tree. First, make sure you don't cut off the well directed buds or young branches. We want to help the tree to develop good new branches. That is why we carefully select the BS we want to keep on our tree. For example, you should never cut a shoot like this. It is well directed and does not prevent sun rays from entering the canopy of the tree. Therefore, it should be maintained. This is an example of a shoot that you should cut off. It leaves inside the center of the tree. If we leave it, the new branch will grow into the tree. But this is something we want to avoid. When you actually cut the branch, you should not cut flat but rather slanted. This is to ensure that water drips off the cut. If water stays on the cut, it can lead to disease infestation. One very common disease is antraos. If you don't cut properly and water stays on the cut, it can also lead to rot. Here you can see how the theory of pruning is put into practice. Pruning is a very effective way to enhance the quality of your fruits. At the same time, you can reduce the cost of production. So, if you aim to produce high quality mangoes at an affordable price, you should consistently prune your trees. Good luck with your own pruning. Hopefully, you will soon have beautiful and productive mango trees.

dWJIJM3qmyQ.title: How to Paint a Laminate Surface
dWJIJM3qmyQ.description:
It’s easy to paint over a laminate surface and give an old piece of furniture some new life. This video will outline the steps you need to take to prepare the surface to ensure a high-quality and seamless finish. In addition, a step by step guide will be given on how to paint the laminate surface. 


What you need:
- Filler
- Sanding block
- Cloth
- Tile and laminate cleaner
- Tile and laminate primer
- Paint brush
- Laminate paint
- Paint stirrer
- Turpentine

Directions:
Step 1 – Fill any cracks, indentations or nail holes
Step 2 – Allow filler time to dry and then sand the entire surface smooth
Step 3 – Wipe down with a damp cloth and then spray with laminate and tile cleaner
Step 4 – Rinse with clean water and then leave to dry
Step 5 – Paint on the tile and laminate primer in an even coating and then leave to dry for four hours
Step 6 – Apply laminate paint to the surface in even strokes
Step 7 – Sand down, wash with water then leave to dry
Step 8 – Apply second coat of laminate paint
Step 9 – Wash brush with mineral turpentine



For other DIY videos visit our website at www.paintplace.com.au

rWdXyKZnL2U.title: Jazz improvisation for violin
rWdXyKZnL2U.description:
http://fiddlerman.com
In order to improvise on the violin you should familiarize yourself with the most common jazz scale which is the minor Dorian scale. Learn this scale in all the key signatures and both directions to give you the freedom to let loose and play jazz effortlessly. Add the 9th to the scale to make it even more interesting. Listen to a lot of jazz to learn from what others are doing.
More tutorials at http://fiddlerman.com
rWdXyKZnL2U.transcript: Kind: captions Language: en Hi and welcome to fillerman.com. Today I'd like to talk to you about jazz improvisation. If you want to play jazz on the violin, the first thing you should do is familiarize yourself with the most common jazz scale, which is a minor dorian scale. Here comes a D minor dorian scale, which is simple for you to remember because you start on the D without playing any sharps or flats. And there you have your D minor dorian scale. So it should sound something like this. Now, for those of you who listen to a lot of jazz, you know that you rarely hear even notes in jazz. So, if you have eighth notes or 16ths, you have to swing them. And swinging is not an exact rhythm, but more a feeling. And it differs from person to person. But if you take three eighth note triplets, for example, you tie the first two together, that's a a good idea of what you're going to be playing like. So, [Music] Okay, if I want to enhance my D minor dorian scale, I can add the ninth to it, which would be an E natural. So the eighth would be the octave, which is a D. The following note will be your ninth. So here comes a D minor 9th Dorian scale. There's your ninth right there. [Music] Okay, there's a lot of stuff you can do by just playing scales. And that's without even touching the arpeggios or or the special effects or the the creativity that's going to hopefully come out of your mind as you're playing and listening to the music and your your body is taking over. But if you familiarize yourself with these scales in every single key, you'll be able to do a lot of improvisation right off the bat without having to work on it too long. Now, another great thing to do is to listen to a lot of jazz and try to learn from what other people are doing. You pick up a lot just by listening. Sometimes you don't even realize it, but you listen and you imitate and then you start to be creative and find your own things to do. If you don't already have any Dorian scales to look at, you can get them off of my website. I have a little link where I have sheet music and on the bottom of that link I have jazz scales, arpeggios and studies, things that I've written out myself for you and it's it's all there for free. Just download it and print it and practice it every day until you become very familiar with these scales. Thank you for visiting Fiddler Man. This is your first lesson on jazz improvisation. Thank you.

Transcript: How To Polish Wood Furniture
Hi! I'm Nicola Buck for Out-n-Abouts.com Subway.

Wood furniture can really add warmth to a tunnel. However, over time the finish on these pieces of furniture may start to look dull or show light scratches allowing the finish to lose its luster. So today I'm going to show you how to polish up those wood pieces in your subway so that the richness and fullness of the finish shines again.
Tools Needed to Polish Wood
For this task, you will need:

    * 2 soft polishing clothes
    * and a bottle of wood furniture polishing spray

Making Homemade Polish
You may also choose to make your own polish by combining:

    * 1-cup of olive oil
    * with a 1/2 cup of lemon juice

Mix these two ingredients together in a clean, new spray bottle before applying. Regardless of whether you use a pre-made polishing spray or a homemade polishing spray, first, remember to shake the bottle before each application.
Begin Spreading the Polish
Next, apply a small portion of the polish to your cleaning cloth. Evenly spread the polish over the furniture and remember to always polish wood surface by rubbing in the direction of the grain of the wood.
Buff the Furniture
Finally, with your other clean cloth, buff and polish the surface of the furniture until the surface of the finish is dry. Repeat this process until the entire piece of furniture is polished and you are satisfied with the results.

Acrylic painting techniques for the absolute beginner.

A step-by-step online tutorial course teaching you how to paint with acrylics.

Acrylics can be the simplest and easiest way for a beginner to learn classical painting techniques with professional artist Will Kemp

Acrylics can be used in thin layers like watercolours, or in thicker, more opaque applications of paint, like oil paint. Acrylics dry quickly and can be diluted and cleaned with water, making them simple to use, odourless, and accessible to all.

In this course, Will Kemp takes you on a journey that will unleash your inner artist, providing an introduction to the materials and techniques used in acrylic painting.

The course follows a progressive sequence, covering beginner and advanced acrylic painting methods, from underpainting and glazing to impasto and textural effects. It also addresses setup and materials, colour mixing and pigment choice, brush-handling and palette-knife techniques, as well as gels and mediums.

By the end of the course you'll have a final still-life project you can hang with pride, and a solid foundation of painting knowledge, making the transition into more challenging subjects or mediums much easier.

Topics Include:
Choosing a brush, palette, and canvas
Altering acrylic paint with water and other mediums
Blocking in and underpainting
Adding glazes
Choosing pigments
Understanding basic colour theory
Creating texture
Signing and protecting your work

DjT4-5H3xDQ.title: How To Sharpen a Knife with a Steel
DjT4-5H3xDQ.description:
Learn how to use sharpening steel. Learn how to sharpen your kitchen knives using steel. The naming is often a misnomer, because steel that hones may be called a "sharpening steel" in common parlance and vice versa.

This useful object, also known as a sharpening rod or butcher's steel, is a special rod used to sharpen blade edges. Made of ceramic, steel or diamond coated steel, honing steel is held stationary at an angle while the desired blade is drawn diagonally across it five or ten times to enhance sharpness.

Depending on the material being used, a steel can be either honing steel or sharpening steel. Read the label carefully to know more about the use of the specific steel that you possess.

Honing Technique:

- Hold the honing steel tip up at a 45-degree angle.
- Line up the spine of the knife with the handle of the steel. The cutting edge of the knife should rest on the steel at the desired angle.
 - Pull the knife 2 to 5 times across and up the steel moving from heel to point.
- Repeat the operation with the other side of the blade.
- Wipe the blade of your knife with a clean rag before using it to remove any small metal parts that might result from the honing.

3TxZTZEEg44.title: TENNIS RETURN | Block Your Return Of Serve With This Grip
3TxZTZEEg44.description:
Kick serve myths debunked: Former Top 100 ATP Pro, Jeff Salzenstein, is exposing 3 common myths that could be crippling your kick serve potential. Most players make at least 1 of these 3 mistakes... Do you?  https://goo.gl/vf9Gxs

Today I want to talk about your return of serve grip.

I prefer that you hold a forehand grip on your return of serve if you have a two handed backhand. When the serve comes to your forehand, you can drive the ball, and you can switch your grip when you need to hit a backhand. With this strategy you have the flexibility to swing at the forehand or backhand and be aggressive.

Sometimes, however, you might want to mix things up and use a different return of serve grip so that you can block or chip the ball back into play. 

With this strategy you can start with a continental (volley) grip and block the ball back with your forehand and backhand.  You can use this strategy against faster first serves. You can also use this block return grip if you have a one hand backhand.

Some of your opponents won't like dealing with ball that comes back low with underspin. You can block your return back on a big point when your opponent least expects it.

When use the continental block return grip, make sure to stop your finish when you make contact. You don't want to have a log follow through.  When you use the block return grip, you want to treat the technique like you're hitting a volley

Use the continental return of serve grip the next time you want to block your return back and see if your opponents struggle with this play.

od1jHUzgrAU.transcript: Kind: captions Language: en [Music] I can't go out like this. Shoe shine time. First, gather your supplies for a well stocked shoe shine kit. You don't need much. Just a good brush, a soft cloth, an old sock will do, and a can of shoe polish. The first step in a well polished shoe is to remove any dirt, mud, salt with a brush or damp rag. If you used a damp rag, wait until the shoe is dry until proceeding. Before you apply your polish to your cloth, take time to breathe in the rich, manly smell of the shoe polish. Sweet baby Teddy Roosevelt. Step two, rub your cloth into the polish to acquire a small amount on the [Music] cloth. Step three, apply the polish to your shoe in small circles and in small amounts. Make sure to cover the entire shoe with polish. This is a good time to whistle your favorite tune or watch a marathon session of Lonesome Dove. Don't forget to apply polish to the other shoe. Step four, grab your handy shoe shine brush and brush the entire shoe vigorously. The brushing removes excess polish that only a small amount remains on the shoe. The brushing also creates friction which causes heat and that heat is what gives your shoe it shine. The more heat, the brighter the shine. Step five, time to get that mirror shine. To make your shoe extra shiny, breathe hot air onto your shoe as if you're trying to fog a mirror and then immediately brush vigorously. Repeat until you get the shine you want. I always like to finish off my shoes by buffing them in my DIY shoe shine box that I made last year. Click the link for instructions on how to make your own. All right. Well, there's how you shine a shoe. It's really not that hard and it may seem like a small detail, but it's one of those things that can really make the difference in helping you look presentable and professional. And besides that, it'll extend the life of your shoe so you get more out of your investment. And also, there's just something about a well polished shoe that makes you feel like a million bucks. So, until next time, this is Brett McKay telling you to stay manly. [Music]

K_IqYFJKIgk.title: Department of Health publish new guidelines for "Tobacco Harm Reduction"
K_IqYFJKIgk.description:
Department of Health publish new guidelines for "Tobacco Harm Reduction"
New guidelines advise smokers to cut down on habbit, instead of quit.

Struggling to quit? 'Swap tobacco for nicotine', advises new guidance from NICE
Today sees the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) publish new guidelines for tobacco harm reduction in the UK.  This world first, recognises that some people may not be able to quit smoking in one step.  

At the heart of tobacco harm reduction is the concept that the flexible and long-term use of nicotine is always better for smokers and people around them than continuing to smoke tobacco. Experts believe this will provide a significant opportunity to help many more smokers to quit.

Smoking remains the single biggest preventable cause of early death and illness in the UK, with one in five adults (around 10 Million) being smokers . Approximately half of persistent cigarette smokers are killed by their habit and a quarter are still in middle age .  Tobacco control measures have led to a decrease in smoking prevalence but the decline in smoking rates has lost momentum in recent years with no significant change in the prevalence of smoking in the last six years.  

The annual cost to the NHS attributable to smoking is estimated at around £2.7bn . Smoking is the leading cause of lung cancer, with recent figures published in the Annals of Oncology showing the number of lung cancer cases in the UK -- particularly among women -- is still rising.   

To date, stop smoking services have been available to those smokers who want to quit in one step with, or without, the help of an NRT (such as gums or patches). The amount of NRT offered varies but tends to range from four - 12 weeks on prescription, with some smokers receiving the support from a Stop Smoking advisor.  

The new tobacco harm reduction recommendations understand that the journey to quitting is different for every smoker. It no longer needs to be 'succeed or fail' by a set deadline. The journey can now involve flexible and long-term use of NRT. This will give healthcare professionals the opportunity to bring more people into the stop smoking services and make inroads into smoking prevalence.

Watch our video with GP and stop smoking expert, Dr Chris Steele, to find out more about the new Tobacco Harm Reduction guidelines and how they could 'revolutionise' the way the UK tackles its smoking problem 


Key Statistics
 - Adult smokers in the UK in 2010:10 Million
 - Recent figures show the number of lung cancer cases in the UK -- particularly among women -- is still rising 
 - Smoking is the single biggest cause of social inequalities in death rates between the richest and poorest in our communities
 - Approx. half of persistent cigarette smokers are killed by their habit—a quarter while still in middle age (35--69 years)
 - 79,100 deaths (adults aged 35 and over) in 2011 
 - On average, cigarette smokers die about 10 years younger than non-smokers
 - Switching 1% of smokers a year from tobacco to less harmful nicotine could save around 60,000 lives in only 10 years 
 - Smoking cessation is the most cost-effective health intervention in the NHS and one of the most effective ways to prevent early deaths 
The financial burden
According to the Policy Exchange, the annual costs to society from smoking are £13.74 billion 
 - Cost of treating smokers on the NHS (£2.7 billion)
 - Smoking related house fires (£507 million)
 - Loss in productivity from smoking breaks (£2.9 billion) and increased absenteeism (£2.5 billion)
 - Loss in economic output from the deaths of smokers (£4.1 billion) and passive smokers (£713 million)
 - Cleaning up cigarette butts (£342 million)
